canonical.title: Network Delay Time
canonical.sourceFilePath: 13. Graphs/4. Shortest Path Problems/07. Network Delay Time.cpp

narrative.title: The Configuration-Propagation Finish Line
narrative.scenario: A cluster controller pushes a config update from one master node across one-way latency links. The rollout finishes when the slowest node has received the update via its cheapest route, so ops needs the maximum, over all nodes, of the shortest latency from the master — or proof that some node can never be reached.
narrative.inputFormat: An integer n (nodes 1..n), a list times where [u, v, w] is a one-way link u -> v costing w, and the originating node k.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the minimum time for every node to receive the signal — the largest shortest-path distance from k — or -1 if some node is unreachable.

testCases.explanation: Nodes 1 and 3 get it in 1 tick; the farthest, node 4, waits 2.
Node 3 never hears anything — the rollout fails.

hintLevels: Level 1: The rollout time is not the longest link — it is the farthest node's cheapest route.
Level 2: Dijkstra from k; the answer is the maximum over all settled distances.
Level 3: An untouched infinity in the distance array is the -1 signal for unreachable nodes.
